text:
The reagent, from the following, which converts benzoic acid to benzaldehyde in one step is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Passing the vapour of a carboxylic acid together with formic acid over $\mathrm{MnO}$ at about $300^{\circ }\text{C}$ converts the acid directly into the aldehyde:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{HCOOH}\leftarrow _{300^{\circ }\text{C}}^{\mathrm{MnO}}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CHO}+\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$\mathrm{LiAlH}{}_{4}$ reduces benzoic acid all the way to benzyl alcohol, $\mathrm{NaBH}{}_{4}$ does not reduce carboxylic acids, and $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$ is an oxidising agent.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text:
The final product 'A' in the following reaction sequence


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
HCN adds to the carbonyl group of butan-2-one to give the cyanohydrin:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}+\mathrm{HCN}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CN}$

Hot concentrated $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ dehydrates the tertiary alcohol to the more substituted alkene, conjugated with the $\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{N}$ group, and hydrolyses the nitrile through the amide to the carboxylic acid:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CN}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{COOH}$

A is 2-methylbut-2-enoic acid; the unsaturated nitrile and the unsaturated amide are only intermediates of this sequence.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text:
CNG is an important transportation fuel. When 100 g CNG is mixed with 208 g oxygen in vehicles, it leads to the formation of $CO_{2}$ and $H_{2}O$ and produces large quantity of heat during this combustion, then the amount of carbon dioxide, produced in grams is $____________$. [nearest integer]

[Assume CNG to be methane]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Initially,

Mass of CNG$(CH_{4}) = 100 gm$

$\therefore$ Moles of $CH_{4} =$ $\frac{100}{16}$ = 6.25 moles

Mass of $O_{2} = 208 gm$

$\therefore$ Moles of $O_{2} =$ $\frac{208}{32}$ = 6.5 moles

From reaction you can see,

1 mole of $CH_{4}$ react with 2 mole of $O_{2}$

$\therefore$ 6.25 mole of $CH_{4}$ react with 6.25 $\times$ 2 = 12.5 moles of $O_{2}$

But here only 6.5 moles of $O_{2}$ present

So, $O_{2}$ will act as limiting reagent.

$\therefore$ Produced $CO_{2}$ will depends on moles of $O_{2}$.

From 2 moles of $O_{2} 1$ mole of $CO_{2}$

$\therefore$ From 6.5 moles of $O_{2}$ $\frac{6.5}{2}$ moles of $CO_{2}$ produced.

$\therefore$ Weight of $CO_{2} =$ $\frac{6.5}{2}$ $\times$ 44 = 143 gm
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text:
A fish swimming in water body when taken out from the water body is covered with a film of water of weight 36 g. When it is subjected to cooking at 100${}^{\circ }$C, then the internal energy for vaporization in kJ mol$^{-1}$ is $___________$. [nearest integer]

[Assume steam to be an ideal gas. Given $\Delta_{vap}$H${}^{\Theta }$ for water at 373 K and 1 bar is 41.1 kJ mol$^{-1}$ ; $R = 8.31 J K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{36\mathrm{g}}(\ell )⟶\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{36\mathrm{g}}(\mathrm{g})$ (evaporation)

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}} & =\dfrac{36}{18}=2\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}=1-0=1 \\  \\ \Delta \mathrm{U}_{\text{vap}} & =\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\text{vap}}-\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}\mathrm{RT} \\  \\ =41.1-(1)\times 8.31\times 10^{-3}\times 373 \\  \\ =41.1-3.099 \\  \\ =38\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift

text:
40% of HI undergoes decomposition to $H_{2}$ and $I_{2}$ at 300 K. $\Delta$G${}^{\Theta }$ for this decomposition reaction at one atmosphere pressure is $__________ J$ mol$^{-1}$. [nearest integer]

(Use $R = 8.31 J K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ ; log 2 = 0.3010, ln 10 = 2.3, log 3 = 0.477)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\therefore$ $K=\frac{\left (\frac{α}{2}\right )^{1/2}\times \left (\frac{α}{2}\right )^{1/2}}{(1-α)}$

Given $α=\frac{40}{100}=0.4$

$\therefore$ $K=\frac{\left (\frac{0.4}{2}\right )^{1/2}\times \left (\frac{0.4}{2}\right )^{1/2}}{(1-0.4)}$

$=\frac{1}{3}$

We know,

$\Delta G^{\circ }=-RT\ln K$

$=-RT\ln \left (\frac{1}{3}\right )$

$=+RT\ln 3$

$=+8.31\times 300\times \ln 3$

= 2735 J/mol

The Gibbs free energy change for the above reaction at 298 K is x $\times$ $10^{-1} kJ$ mol$^{-1}$. The value of x is $__________$. [nearest integer]

solution.body: $\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{Cu} & +\mathrm{Sn}^{+2}⟶\mathrm{Cu}^{+2}+\mathrm{Sn}(\mathrm{s}) \\  \\ \mathrm{E}_{\text{cell}}^{\circ } & =\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{OX}}^{\circ }+\mathrm{E}_{\text{Red}}^{\circ } \\  \\ =-0.34-0.14 \\  \\ =-0.48\mathrm{V} \\  \\ \mathrm{E}= & \mathrm{E}^{\circ }-\dfrac{0.0591}{2}\log \dfrac{\left [\mathrm{Cu}^{+2}\right ]}{\left [\mathrm{Sn}^{+2}\right ]} \\  \\ = & -0.48-0.0295\log 10 \\  \\ = & -0.5095\mathrm{V} \\  \\ \Delta \mathrm{G}= & -\mathrm{nFE} \\  \\ =-2\times 96500\times -0.5095\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{mol} \\  \\ =98333.5\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol} \\  \\ =983.3\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol} \\  \\ =983\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol} \end{array}$

text:
Catalyst A reduces the activation energy for a reaction by 10 kJ mol$^{-1}$ at 300 K. The ratio of rate constants, $\frac{{}^{k}T,Catalysed}{{}^{k}T,Uncatalysed}$ is $e^{x}$. The value of x is $___________$. [nearest integer]

[Assume that the pre-exponential factor is same in both the cases. Given $R = 8.31 J K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Activation Energy : It is the minimum amount of energy required to activate the molecules/ atoms so that they can undergo the chemical reaction.

A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by lowering the activation energy so that more reactant molecules collide with enough energy to surmount the smaller energy barrier.

In the Question,

Given : $\mathrm{E}_{\text{cat}}-\mathrm{E}_{\text{uncat}}=10\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}$

$\mathrm{T}=300\mathrm{K}$

According to Arrhenius Equation,

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{K}=A\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{Ea}/\mathrm{RT}} \\  \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{E}_{\text{cat}}}{\mathrm{E}_{\text{uncat}}}=e^{\frac{Ea-E1a}{RT}} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =e^{\frac{10\times 10 3}{8.21\times 300}} \\  \\ =e^{4} \\  \\ =4 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Evening Shift
